- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth.
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- Model consistently underestimates price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for such cases.
- If recent 18-day price trend is steeply downward and sentiment is negative, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overestimates volatility in early horizon when sentiment is volatile — smooth forecast curve by reducing amplitude of short-term swings.
- When sentiment turns positive after a sharp drop, model often lags — forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- In cases of strong sentiment reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model tends to delay response — add 1–3 days lag to forecast adjustment.
